headline: CCRI, URI launch online degree path for Rhode Island nurses
dek: The new RN-to-BS program lets eligible CCRI nursing alumni pursue a bachelor’s degree online while continuing to work, with lower tuition and scholarship opportunities highlighted by the schools.
body: The Community College of Rhode Island and the University of Rhode Island have launched a fully online pathway for registered nurses who want to earn a Bachelor of Science degree without stepping away from their jobs. The schools announced the RN-to-BS program after an Oct. 1 signing ceremony in Warwick, describing it as a response to the state’s need for a stronger and more flexible nursing pipeline. [URI’s announcement](https://www.uri.edu/news/2026/10/uri-ccri-announce-new-rn-to-bs-program-to-strengthen-rhode-islands-nursing-workforce/) was posted Oct. 2.

The program is aimed at graduates of CCRI’s Associate Degree in Nursing program and is designed around the schedules of practicing nurses. URI and CCRI say the new track combines online coursework with a lower tuition rate for the RN-to-BS program and scholarship opportunities. That matters in a workforce where returning to school can otherwise require a nurse to reduce hours, commute to campus or delay further education until family and work responsibilities ease.

The schools say the arrangement can begin before students finish their associate-level training. Eligible CCRI nursing students may receive conditional admission to URI after completing their first full semester in CCRI’s nursing program, then move into URI’s bachelor’s curriculum after graduation. CCRI graduates who are already working can apply through URI Online; the program’s admissions page says applicants generally need an associate degree or diploma from an ACEN-accredited nursing program, a 2.6 minimum cumulative grade-point average and an active, unrestricted U.S. nursing license. CCRI students in their final semester may apply before submitting that license, but must provide proof of licensure by the end of their first URI semester. [URI’s program page](https://web.uri.edu/online/programs/undergraduate/nursing-rn-to-bs/) says the degree is an education pathway and does not itself lead to professional licensure.

URI’s published program information lists 24 core credit hours that can be completed in as little as 15 months, while the full bachelor’s degree requires 120 total credits after nursing, general education, statistics and pharmacology requirements are met. The school lists a current tuition figure of $631 per credit based on the 2025-26 academic year and notes that rates can change. Students from Rhode Island, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Jersey and New York are currently eligible to apply through URI Online, subject to the program’s other requirements.

The partnership gives the state’s two public institutions a shared way to connect community-college nursing preparation with a four-year degree. URI nursing Dean Danny Willis said in the university announcement that baccalaureate-prepared nurses are associated with improved quality and safety outcomes, including lower risks of mortality and hospital readmission in research cited by the program. Those findings are presented by the university as part of the case for expanding the number of nurses with bachelor’s degrees; they are not a guarantee about outcomes for any individual hospital or graduate.

[Providence Business News](https://pbn.com/ccri-uri-launch-online-degree-pathway-for-registered-nurses/) independently reported that the pathway will allow CCRI associate-degree nursing graduates to move into URI’s bachelor’s curriculum online while continuing to work. The newspaper also identified Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee, state Sen. Hanna Gallo and state Rep. David Bennett among officials connected to the announcement. The next practical step for prospective students is to review URI’s admissions requirements and the Nov. 24 application deadline listed on the program page for classes beginning Jan. 5, 2027.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: CCRI, URI launch online RN-to-BS path for Rhode Island nurses
seoDescription: CCRI and URI launched a fully online RN-to-BS pathway for eligible Rhode Island nursing alumni, with lower tuition and scholarships.
